Walleye fishing continued to be excellent this past week. The fish had moved slightly deeper, with anglers having the most success northeast of Bolles Harbor in 20 to 24 feet of water using both bottom bouncers and crankbaits.
Some anglers caught a few yellow perch while targeting walleye with crawlers, although it was still early in the season for them to be fully schooled up. Many catfish were caught out in the DTE hot ponds using natural bait.
The Detroit River also continued to produce walleye, with many anglers catching fish there and bringing them to the Sterling State Park Fish Cleaning Station. Shore fishing in the lagoons at the state park was also very good for panfish, bass, and catfish. Both lures and natural baits were effective there. The best colors for harnesses and lures for walleye were green and orange.

Anglers fishing for bass in the lower Saginaw River caught both smallmouth and largemouth bass while casting artificial baits around structure and rocky areas. They also caught the occasional northern pike and walleye. Other anglers fishing with nightcrawlers on the bottom caught mostly freshwater drum and channel catfish.

Fishing around Quanicassee produced walleye in 12 to 14 feet of water and in as shallow as 6 feet. Some anglers also caught walleye around Callahan Reef and the southern end of the slot.
From Sunset Marina to Sebewaing, anglers caught walleye off the bar and along the edges where it dropped off into 20 to 24 feet of water. Some walleye were also caught in deeper water around 26 feet east of the shipping channel. A few large yellow perch were mixed in with the walleye. Body baits and crawler harnesses both produced fish in a variety of colors.

Walleye anglers were successful at Callahan Reef, trolling in 9 to 12 feet of water using crawler harnesses. Anglers also caught fish near Sparkplug while trolling in 23 feet of water with flicker shads, and 3 miles northeast of the area while trolling with flicker shads. Additional success was reported by anglers trolling in front of Linwood in 18 to 22 feet of water using crawler harnesses.
Fishing pressure was light. Anglers fishing in the vicinity of Caldwell Boat Launch caught freshwater drum and channel catfish while fishing with nightcrawlers on the bottom.

Salmon anglers reported another good week of fishing. The salmon fishing got tougher the last couple of days; 75 to 100 feet of water was the most consistent. Standard sized spoons worked best. Pier anglers caught a few steelhead and a decent number of freshwater drum. Most of the fish were caught on shrimp or alewife. Perch fishing pressure was very low.

Salmon fishing was slow with fish being reported as spread out. Anglers caught fish from 55 feet of water out well beyond 120 feet of water. The most consistent water was around 80 feet. Pier fishing was steady. Steelhead were caught on shrimp as well as live bait and by casting.
Good numbers of walleye were caught in the lower St Joseph river by anglers trolling crank baits and drifting crawlers.

Salmon fishing slowed down slightly over the past week but a fair number were still caught. Salmon were scattered in 60 to 220 feet of water with the best action reported in 70 to 140 feet of water. Green and orange spoons worked well with a few caught on white flasher-flies.

Boat anglers noticed the salmon action slowing down over the past week. They still caught a fair number of salmon in addition to a few steelhead 30 to 100 feet down in 60 to 140 feet of water. Spoons did the best in the colors of orange, yellow, and green. Pier anglers targeting steelhead found the action to be slow. Anglers casting the in the channel for freshwater drum caught a few on silver spoons.

Smallmouth bass were caught and released by boat anglers. Those fishing from shore at the Tawas River mouth reported slow fishing overall with only a few freshwater drum and catfish being caught.
In Au Gres, Boat anglers fishing straight out of Au Gres caught some walleye with numbers averaging at two to five fish per boat in around 28 feet of water. Boat anglers heading out from the Pine River seemed to see better numbers trolling the shallower water. Both crawlers and body baits produced catches. Northern pike, channel catfish, freshwater drum and white bass were also caught. Shore anglers targeting panfish reported slow fishing.

Walleye anglers reported success in Thunder Bay while trolling crankbaits during low-light conditions. Crawler harnesses had hit-or-miss success during the day in 12 to 20 feet of water. With high winds, fish were scattered throughout the bay.
Anglers fishing 40 to 80 feet of water had success with lake trout using spoons and Spin-N-Glos fished lower in the water column. Atlantic salmon and a few coho salmon were taken on spoons fished higher in the water column, with orange, watermelon, and chartreuse proving productive.
Smallmouth bass were found in 5 to 10 feet of water, with white, black, and silver jigs working well.

Decent numbers of walleye were caught throughout the river on jigs, crawlers, and body baits. Natural colors worked best throughout the day. Atlantic salmon were caught while casting smaller body baits and spinners in blue/silver, green/silver, and gold. Good numbers of catfish were taken by anglers fishing with crawlers on the bottom during the evenings and after dark.

Atlantic salmon were caught from shore on minnows as well as small spoons. Boat anglers reported success on lake trout in 25 to 80 feet of water. Fish remained well scattered, with water temperatures in the mid-40s. Spoons in chartreuse, white, and watermelon were productive, as well as dodgers and Spin-N-Glos. A few steelhead were taken while fishing bright-colored spoons high in the water column. Bass anglers reported decent smallmouth fishing near Bell Bay in 5 to 10 feet of water while using plastic swimbaits.

The Cheboygan Lock and Dam Complex remains closed to the public. Lake trout were plentiful this past week. Anglers were very successful at Poe Reef, Reynolds Reef, and Cordwood Point in 40 to 60 feet of water. They primarily hit spoons, with occasional catches on Spin-N-Glos and flashers. Productive colors included green, yellow, and orange.
In the Cheboygan River, walleye and steelhead were reported. Walleye reports increased as the week progressed. Shore anglers drifted various combinations of jigs and live bait, while boat anglers drifted nightcrawlers exclusively. Some anglers came close to their bag limits for walleye, although most caught one fish per trip.
Steelhead anglers were successful while drifting beads. Both walleye and steelhead were caught between the State Street drawbridge and the Cheboygan pedestrian walkway bridge.

Anglers casting bandits and deep husky jerks off the pierhead found some walleye. Anglers trolling scatter raps in the lower river and around the pierhead picked up walleye. A handful of Atlantic salmon were taken by anglers drifting minnows under a bobber in the lower river. Lake trout fishing was reported great with limits being taken in 50 to 70 feet of water on spoons and dodgers/Spin-N-Glos. A handful of coho salmon, steelhead and pink salmon were also caught by anglers trolling spoons.

Anglers casting in the harbor caught pike and smallmouth. Anglers targeting lake trout in 50 to 65 feet of water did well this week on spoons and Spin-N-Glos. A few coho salmon, Atlantic salmon and steelhead were also caught in 50 to 65 feet of water.

Lake trout were plentiful, and many anglers limited out. The best depths were 30 to 70 feet of water. Running lines throughout the water column produced the best results. Attractors with Spin-N-Glos worked well in the bottom 10 feet. Spoons were also productive, particularly in green, blue, orange, and yellow colors. Lead cores, downriggers, and dipsy divers were all effective.
Some Atlantic salmon were also caught in the top 30 feet of the water column. Anglers had success using brightly colored, smaller spoons.

Lake trout fishing was very good, and most anglers limited out. The best depths were 40 to 90 feet of water. Anglers ran lines throughout the water column for the best results. Spoons, as well as attractors with Spin-N-Glos or Spin-N-Glo flies, were productive. Effective colors included green, blue, white, yellow, orange, gold, and copper.
There were occasional catches of steelhead, coho salmon, and Chinook salmon. The Atlantic salmon were found in the top 20 feet of the water column, while the other silver species were caught by running lines throughout the water column.

Boat anglers caught Chinook salmon and lake trout along the shelf in 120 to 230 feet of water while trolling spoons and flasher-fly combos 50 to 70 feet down. Pier anglers caught chinook salmon while casting spoons in the mornings. The south pier is currently closed due to construction.

Chinook salmon were caught at and around Big Sable point in 50 to 200 feet of water while fishing 25 to 90 feet down, Northwest of town in 50 to 60 feet of water, 30 feet down, and south in 40 to 60 feet of water. Spoons worked best but flasher-fly combos also caught fish. In the mix came a few suspended lake trout, coho salmon and steelhead. Fish were mostly scattered and fishing was slightly slower this week. A few Chinook salmon were caught off the piers while casting spoons in the early mornings. There were plenty of alewife in the harbor, but those fishing bait had little luck.

Anglers targeting cisco reported decent numbers early in the morning and throughout the day. Casting and jigging small spoons produced the best results. Those fishing from boats also reported decent numbers of cisco, as well as a few scattered lake trout.
Anglers fishing the Bear River reported low numbers of dark steelhead. Beads and flies produced the occasional bite. Those targeting lake trout reported low numbers of fish west of Harbor Springs.

Anglers targeting smallmouth bass had success while casting along the breaks in 5 to 15 feet of water. Lake trout were caught by those jigging around Power Island in 50 to 100 feet of water. Water temperatures varied from low 40s in the north to mid 50s in the southern areas of the bay.

Smallmouth bass were caught in 5 to 10 feet of water. Anglers using swimbaits and tubes had success as the bass moved into shallower water to spawn. The water temperature averaged 50 degrees throughout the bay. A few lake trout were caught around Deepwater Point by anglers jigging in 15 to 50 feet of water. Both lake trout and smallmouth bass were caught in the Elk River. As water temperatures increased, more smallmouth bass entered the river.

Boat anglers had the most success targeting lake trout while trolling second bank in 100 to 150 feet of water, bait depth seemed to vary from 90 to 110 feet down with greens and orange being the best colors. Anglers reported large patches of bait fish while trolling. Pier anglers targeted smallmouth bass, with little success.

Anglers reported good numbers of Chinook salmon from the herring hole to Platte Bay as alewife were plentiful throughout the area. Trolling from 40 to 100 feet down with spoons were successful, but some larger Chinook salmon were caught on meat rigs. Pier anglers reported catches on both casting and live bait.
Lake trout anglers jigging in Platte Bay reported good numbers of fish in 40 to 70 feet of water off the bottom.
Anglers went straight out from the pier heads to 80 to 100 feet of water trolling the top 60 feet reporting a few Chinook salmon in the early mornings.
Boat anglers in Suttons Bay and around Stony Point caught lake trout while jigging white tubes and spoons. Smallmouth bass anglers reported some success while fishing in Onema Bay and Suttons Bay.

Smallmouth bass anglers reported good fishing this week. While most fish had moved off their beds, anglers were still able to have success fishing relatively shallow water. Some bass anglers found vegetation at the bottom of drop-offs, as well as rocky areas, where the bass were feeding on goby.
Walleye anglers reported fair to good fishing. Some anglers fished the head of the bay with some success; however, the action slowed somewhat this week. Elsewhere, anglers reported good fishing farther south, including around Escanaba and points south. Successful trips were also reported from areas near Fox Park. Anglers trolled crawler harnesses and crankbaits, while others had success casting toward drop-offs and flats.
Perch anglers reported mixed results. Many anglers experienced limited success, while others reported that although the schools were somewhat spread out and difficult to locate, they were still able to have productive trips. Slip bobbers and perch rigs baited with minnows and worms were the most common presentations.

Boat anglers trolling the bay and around Grand Island did very well on Chinook salmon, with a few coho salmon mixed in. Anglers targeting lake trout also had success while trolling and jigging around Grand Island. A few splake were reported caught off the Anna River Mouth.

Anglers reported fair to good numbers of coho salmon and lake trout being caught while trolling stickbaits, spoons, and flasher-fly combinations in the upper 30 feet of the water column. Anglers also caught king salmon and rainbow trout while trolling, although in smaller numbers. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite, with most fish being caught on natural bait.

Anglers trolling near structure reported good numbers of lake trout and a few coho salmon while using stickbaits and spoons. Anglers also reported occasional catches of brown trout. Anglers targeting lake trout reported a good bite while jigging both natural and artificial baits in more than 100 feet of water, with the greatest success occurring around 150 feet.

The river saw healthy fishing efforts over the past week. Reports show that walleye were caught in fair numbers. Trolling was the most successful fishing method for anglers. Shore anglers reported less frequent catches of walleye as well as occasional rock bass.

Fishing efforts were fair out of Silver city and Union Bay. Ontonagon experienced very high efforts due to the Ontonagon Lake Trout Classic fishing tournament held over this past weekend. Reports from anglers included catches of coho salmon, Chinook salmon, brown trout, and lake trout in good numbers. Trolling in shallow waters resulted in the best yields for boat anglers. Shore anglers fishing from these ports reported catches of coho salmon and brown trout in low numbers.

The harbor saw a fair amount of angling efforts over the past week. Recent reports suggest that fishing was hit or miss. Some anglers caught limits followed by low action on the next day with similar conditions. Boat anglers reported mixed catches of coho salmon, brown trout, Chinook salmon, and lake trout in varying numbers. Anglers fishing within the harbor and from the break walls reported catches of coho salmon in low numbers.

Anglers fishing off the breakwall found some lake whitefish and round whitefish toward evening, with spawn and worms working best as bait. Boating anglers reported good success on lake trout while trolling and jigging.

Anglers in Hessel caught a few small perch in the club cut. Smallmouth bass began moving onto beds, and anglers had success catching them in the shallows around the islands and in the shallow bays throughout Hessel and Cedarville. Pike were also caught off the wall in Hessel, mostly on chubs. Perch were hard to come by off the docks in Hessel.
Hill Island also produced a few bass and pike. Atlantic salmon were still present around the marina in Hessel, but anglers had a difficult time getting them to commit.
In DeTour Village, fishing pressure had just begun to pick up. Fishing was still relatively slow, with only a few anglers having success catching Atlantic salmon. Those who were successful reported that the fish were holding high in the water column.

Slow to fair fishing for walleye anglers. Anglers used worms and cast into river holes, with some trolling with crank baits. There were many reports of smallmouth and northern pike catches throughout the river. Anglers targeting lake trout and salmon reported slow fishing.

Brown trout continued to be consistent with both boater anglers and river anglers in the Chocolay River. In the lower harbor, the coho salmon bite remained hit or miss this week depending on the water temperatures, but there have been a good number of Chinook salmon caught all over Marquette and out towards Shot Point in around 30 to 40 feet of water.

Coho salmon, Chinook salmon, and brown trout fishing was reported as good. In Au Train Bay, there were several Chinook salmon caught by Scott Falls and up towards the tip of 5 Mile Point this week in around 40 feet of water. The lake trout were targeted by anglers jigging and trolling this week North of Au Train Island.

When fish seem difficult to locate, use your electronics to find baitfish first. Predator species such as walleye, salmon, trout, and bass are often nearby. Spending a few extra minutes searching for bait schools can save hours of unproductive fishing and help you concentrate your efforts in the most productive areas.
This report is intended to give you an idea of fishing conditions around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams in Michigan, not all locations can be listed.

Yellow perch fishing remained slow over the past week. Anglers caught many small perch that were thrown back, with roughly a one-to-one ratio of kept fish to released fish. Perch anglers had more success out from Luna Pier in around 15 to 18 feet of water than out from the River Raisin. Jigging with minnows was the most effective method. Walleye fishing on the Michigan side was slow for most part; however, a few boat anglers found fish east of Stony Point along the Michigan-Ohio line using crawler harnesses, though success was very infrequent.

Walleye fishing was slow over the weekend, though a few were caught out in front of Pinconning and by the slot in 18 to 20 feet of water.
Yellow perch anglers caught fish around the sailboat buoys, with buoy B being productive. Anglers averaged about 10 to 12 keeper-sized perch per boat, ranging from 10 to 12 inches, along with a high number of throwbacks.

Anglers caught some walleye, though fishing was slower overall. Most anglers fished half a day to land six to eight walleye per boat. Walleye were found in the slot off Sebewaing and Fish Point in 15 feet of water, as well as out toward the shipping channel near Buoy 1, where trolling nightcrawler harnesses worked best. Anglers also found a few yellow perch in the slot south of Sebewaing in 13 feet of water, noting that moving often helped locate active fish.

Boat anglers reported salmon 50 to 85 feet down in 100 to 140 feet of water. The best bait continued to be glow spoons and glow plugs during low-light conditions. Anglers targeting salmon were unsuccessful due to warm water, though a few freshwater drum were caught using spoons or swimbaits.

Salmon were caught 50 to 90 feet down in 85 to 150 feet of water. Blue and green spoons worked well, along with a white flasher-fly combo. Due to increasing water temperatures, no salmon or steelhead were reported from the pier. A few freshwater drum were caught while casting spoons.
A fair number of salmon were reported 45 to 90 feet down in 100 to 130 feet of water. Green or blue glow spoons worked well. Pier anglers caught a few freshwater drum while casting spoons.

Boat anglers found salmon along with a few steelhead 55 to 80 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water. White flasher-fly combinations and glow spoons produced the most bites. Pier anglers caught freshwater drum and catfish in the channel.

Walleye were caught in good numbers in 40 to 60 feet of water near Charity Island and in the Alabaster area. Crawler harnesses and crankbaits both produced fish.
Decent numbers of walleye were caught in 25 to 34 feet of water straight out front in Au Gres and to the south. Crawler harnesses produced the best results. Anglers reported walleye, freshwater drum, white perch, white bass, and an occasional yellow perch.

Walleye fishing in the bay was reported as slow. Those targeting walleye had success in 30 to 60 feet of water from North Point to Scarecrow Island. Lake trout were caught in 100 to 130 feet of water in the bottom 30 feet. A few steelhead were also caught while trolling bright-colored spoons in the top 25 feet of the water column.
Walleye fishing was reported slow. A few smallmouth bass were caught while casting spinners. Catfish were plentiful throughout the river while fishing crawlers on bottom.

Lake trout fishing remained solid in 100 to 150 feet of water. Flashers with Spin-N-Glos and spoons worked well, with chartreuse, white, and green yielding the best results. A few Chinook salmon and coho salmon were caught east of Middle Island in 120 to 180 feet of water, with spoons, meat rigs, and flasher-fly combos producing the best results. Steelhead were caught near the surface on orange, gold, and watermelon spoons. Walleye were scattered from Stoneport to South 9 Mile Point, 5 to 30 feet down in over 40 to 60 feet of water. Anglers had success running lines through the water column using crankbaits and crawler harnesses.

Lake trout were caught off the northeastern points of Bois Blanc Island and across all major reefs, including Poe Reef, Raynolds Reef, and Spectacle Reef. Spoons produced the best bite, though lake trout were occasionally caught using flashers and Spin-N-Glos in over 100 feet of water. An occasional Chinook salmon was also caught while trolling spoons.
Low numbers of smallmouth bass and rock bass were reported in the lower Cheboygan River by anglers drifting nightcrawlers. Smallmouth bass were occasionally caught using swimbaits and spinnerbaits.

Anglers did well on walleye when trolling spoons in 80 to 150 feet of water, 20 to 50 feet down. Lake trout were also taken on spoons and Spin-N-Glos. A few steelhead were caught throughout the water column. Anglers fishing off the catwalk/pier caught channel catfish and freshwater drum using pyramid weights and nightcrawlers. A few nice smallmouth bass were caught on swimbaits and tubes.

Anglers trolling spoons and Spin-N-Glos in 90 to 130 feet of water caught lake trout in the bottom 20 feet of water. Walleye were also caught on spoons 20 to 50 feet down. Anglers casting in the harbor caught a few northern pike on spinnerbaits.

Salmon fishing remained abnormally slow and failed to show any improvement. The best bite occurred very early or very late in the day. Anglers headed south toward Swan Bay and Adams Point for the best results, with optimal depths ranging anywhere from 40 to 90 feet of water. Anglers used an assortment of spoons, J-plugs, meat rigs, and flashers with plastic squids or flies. Effective colors included green, blue, yellow, white UV, and glow patterns for early-morning and late-evening fishing.
Walleye continued to be an incidental catch for anglers targeting salmon and lake trout. Lake trout were found deep in over 100 feet of water, seeking cold water and becoming more structure-oriented along with the cold water trends.

Warm water was present throughout the area up until150 feet of water. Salmon were difficult to find, but lake trout fishing was reported good out deep off the hump, where they were caught near the bottom in cold water. Salmon were caught high in the water column, along with incidental catches of walleye, requiring lines spread throughout the water column. Anglers used spoons, flashers with flies or squids, meat rigs, and J-Plugs. Effective colors included white UV, green, blue, and glow patterns for early-morning and late-evening fishing.

Anglers targeting Chinook salmon found them in 80 to 140 feet of water, straight out and south of the port, while trolling plugs, spoons, and flasher-fly combos 50 to 60 feet down. Chinook salmon were also caught in 170 to 220 feet of water while fishing 50 to 80 feet down, with a few coho salmon and steelhead in the mix. Anglers fishing the piers caught largemouth bass, smallmouth bass, northern pike, walleye, and a couple of Chinook salmon while casting spoons and lures. Early mornings and late evenings produced the best bite, with glow, green, and blue colors working best.

Chinook salmon were caught out from the projects in 80 to 110 feet of water while trolling 40 to 60 feet down, as well as at Big Sable Point in 70 to 180 feet of water while fishing the top 60 feet with plugs, spoons, flasher-fly combos, and meat rigs. Warm water slowed action on the pier and in Pere Marquette Lake. Green and glow colors worked well.

Boat anglers targeting salmon found slow but steady success trolling in 90 to 140 feet of water. Running lines at the temperature break, roughly 65 to 85 feet down, produced the best results. Anglers used blue, green, and silver spoons, flasher-flies, and the occasional meat rig. Smallmouth bass fishing on the pier produced several small, undersized fish.

Anglers targeting salmon found most catches on the Petoskey side of the bay. Targeting fish at the temperature break, roughly 65 to 85 feet down, produced slow but steady results. Occasional lake trout were also caught.

Anglers fishing out of Elk Rapids caught lake trout while trolling roughly 80 feet down in 100 to 120 feet of water. A few Chinook salmon were also reported, though the salmon bite remained inconsistent. White and green flasher-fly combinations worked well. Anglers trolling around Old Mission also caught lake trout in 70 to 130 feet of water. Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught good numbers of lake trout when trolling in 80 to 140 feet of water. Water temperatures throughout the bay hovered between 70 and 73 degrees. Smallmouth bass were caught in the Elk River.

Lake trout were caught by anglers trolling in 100 to 140 feet of water along the west bank just north of Elmwood Marina, with a few Chinook salmon also in the mix. A combination of spoons and flasher-fly setups worked well. Smallmouth bass fishing slowed, but those fishing along the breaks in 20 to 40 feet of water landed some quality-sized fish. Water temperatures hovered between 69 and 73 degrees.

Boat anglers trolling for salmon reported excellent numbers of fish caught at North Manitou Island. Anglers reported the best water being 130 to 300 feet of water 60 to 90 feet down. Boat anglers who reached the island reported starting a north troll on the southeast side and following the banks. Anglers reported marking tons of bait fish while catching steelhead 40 to 60 feet down. Anglers fishing both the first and second banks reported harvesting a few Chinook salmon while trolling. Effective bait included green and blue spoons, as well as natural and artificial meat rigs. Water temperatures were in the mid-60s down to 70 feet, where temperatures then dropped to 45 degrees. The best times for fishing were before sunrise and right before sunset.

The Chinook salmon bite was in full swing, with several anglers reporting limits during the early morning bite before sunup and very good catches during the evening. Anglers set lines in 120 to 200 feet of water and worked the temperature break 50 to 70 feet down. “Bloody nose” colored spoons and plugs produced very good numbers of fish. Coho salmon moved into the area, resulting in more knockoffs. Steelhead hit well in the top 30 feet of water on orange spoons. Anglers jigging reported low catch numbers, though Chinook salmon were reported in the Betsie River.

The early morning bite in front of the golf course and working the Barrel after sunrise worked well for anglers targeting Chinook salmon. For evening fishing, anglers headed straight out to 180 to 220 feet of water, trolling north as they set lines working the top 100 feet of water.

Anglers reported targeting lake trout by jigging and trolling near Stony Point, Omena Bay, and the areas surrounding Northport. Jigging with small white and gold spoons worked the best. Pier anglers caught small rock bass.

Anglers targeting walleye trolled with planer boards and crawler harnesses. Some anglers reported success using crankbaits, with the best results coming at low speeds. Anglers who traveled south into Green Bay had fair success, while others who used reaction baits fished near the bottom. Yellow perch anglers reported inconsistent fishing, though some caught fish near Escanaba Harbor and the Escanaba River.

Boat anglers trolling and jigging for lake trout around Wood and Grand Island had good success. Boat anglers trolling the bay caught a few splake. Anglers targeting splake reported a slow bite off the Anna River mouth.

Over the past week, the river continued to see a fair-to-low amount of angling effort. Reports from anglers included catches of walleye in low numbers. Anglers reported having better luck catching fish when jigging, as opposed to trolling. Occasional catches of lake sturgeon were reported by those fishing with natural baits. Shore anglers reported catches of walleye, rock bass, and lake sturgeon in low numbers. Reports suggested that morning hours were the most productive time of day for catching these fish.

Angling effort from Ontonagon was somewhat low over the past week. Effort from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites increased from previous weeks but remained lower than in Ontonagon. Reports from anglers included catches composed primarily of lake trout in fair-to-low numbers. Occasional catches of brown trout were reported at a much lower frequency. Anglers reported trolling across depths varying anywhere from 80 to 180 feet of water.

The harbor continued to see low angling effort over the past week. Anglers reported catches of lake trout in low numbers. Reports found that anglers trolled in depths of 80 to 180 feet of water to find these fish. Shore anglers within the harbor boundaries had very little success.

Anglers who trolled spoons off St. Martin’s islands and the coast guard pier had limited success catching Chinook salmon.
Anglers drifting leeches for walleye at the Carp and Pine rivers had mixed results.
Boat anglers continued doing well trolling and jigging for lake trout, with a few reports of coho salmon caught while trolling. Anglers fishing off the break wall had little success.

Anglers targeted Chinook salmon south of Manistique and near the Garden Peninsula in depths of 90 feet of water and deeper. Spoons produced fish, although anglers also reported success with flasher-flies and meat rigs. Salmon were still present. Steelhead were also caught, typically on lures fished higher in the water column.

Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks in 120 to 160 feet of water for lake trout. They reported catching fish throughout the water column, though the larger lake trout were found in slightly deeper water near Granite Rock. A few anglers reported catching small numbers of salmon and brown trout near Little Presque Isle and the Clay Banks in roughly 60 to 100 feet of water. Few anglers ventured out to Sand River and Shot Point, as lake trout and brown trout catches declined compared to the previous week.

Angling effort was low in Au Train this week due to the weather, with only two anglers interviewed. They reported fishing in 120 to 160 feet of water. Lake trout were caught near the bottom, northwest of Au Train Island or by Wood Island Reef.

Anglers reported fair fishing over the past week, with most of the catch composed of lake trout. Anglers also reported catching a few smaller Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and rainbow trout. Trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations produced the most results. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite, landing fish on natural and artificial presentations across varying depths throughout the week.
Fishing activity was more consistent with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers did best jigging in 15 to 20 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations near structure in 60 to 100 feet of water reported fair to good numbers of lake trout. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported a fair bite when using natural and artificial bait. Most fish were caught between 100 and 140 feet of water with some anglers reporting success in waters deeper than 200 feet.

Anglers in Hessel caught salmon as well as lake trout out of the west entrance. Anglers reported a few perch from the marina docks. There were reports of good numbers of smaller northern pike around the marina as well as in wilderness bay. In DeTour, anglers caught lake trout by trolling the flats. Chinook salmon and Atlantic salmon were reported caught by anglers trolling around the lighthouse in the early mornings and late afternoons.

Many anglers would agree there’s an excitement that comes when you’re using topwater techniques to target bass. There’s something to be said for seeing a bass strike your lure with your own two eyes.
But how do you fish for this species on top of the water? It mostly comes down to location and lure selection.
Target areas that provide good cover for the bass that have a few feet of water over them, such as weedbeds, logs, big rocks, etc. Cast a floating lure next to the cover and play with it a bit before reeling it in.
When it comes to lures, select those that float and are designed to resemble the favorite foods of bass, such as frogs.
Also, top water fishing for bass works best in low-light conditions such as early in the morning or late in the evening.
Learn more about bass fishing at Michigan.gov/FishID .
This report is intended to give you an idea of what is going on around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams, not all locations can be listed. However, it is safe to say if a species is being caught in some waters in the area, they are likely being caught in all waters in that section of the state that have that species.

Yellow perch fishing remained slow throughout the area. Many small yellow perch were caught and released. No specific location outperformed another. Walleye were found in deeper water with slow action reported. Anglers targeting perch found a few opportunities near the mouth of the River Raisin.

Walleye continued to be caught, though limits were scarce. Boats averaged 5 to 6 fish, with some doing better. Productive locations included Callahan Reef in 14 feet of water, as well as further out in the vicinity of the Spark Plug and Buoys #1 and #2 in the shipping channel, where anglers did best trolling nightcrawler harnesses.
Anglers reported success targeting smallmouth bass in the Grand River.

Boat anglers caught fair numbers of Chinook salmon along with some coho salmon and steelhead. The best action was 50 to 100 feet down in 90 to 170 feet of water. Glow spoons and glow plugs worked well. Boat anglers targeted 90 to 120 feet of water range at first light. Early morning was more productive than the evening. Pier anglers caught a few freshwater drum, with no salmon reported from the piers.

Boat anglers found decent numbers of salmon 55 to 100 feet down in 90 to 120 feet of water. Anglers venturing offshore found a mix of steelhead and coho salmon in 200 to 250 feet of water. The morning bite was very good compared to the evening bite. Glow plugs worked well in low-light conditions. Pier anglers caught a few bass and freshwater drum on ned rigs, with no salmon reported from the piers.

Boat anglers reported limited success while trolling nightcrawlers and crankbaits in 25 to 30 feet of water. Fish were scattered from North Point to as far south as Scarecrow Island. Anglers targeting trout or salmon reported little success. A few northern pike were caught close to the pier in the weedbeds while casting large spinnerbaits and jerkbaits.

Walleye fishing was reported as very slow. Smallmouth bass were caught while casting spinners and smaller spinnerbaits. Northern pike were also caught throughout the river on spinners, crankbaits, and spinnerbaits. Catfish were found in good numbers throughout the river while using cut bait and nightcrawlers fished on the bottom.

Anglers found walleye from Stoneport to South Nine-Mile Point. Both crankbaits and nightcrawlers found success while trolling in 20 to 50 feet of water. Lake trout were plentiful in 80 to 140 feet of water straight out of the harbor. Dodgers and Spin-N-Glos, as well as spoons, worked well when fished close to the bottom. Anglers also reported a few Chinook salmon, coho salmon, and steelhead in the same waters. Spoons in green, watermelon, orange, and chartreuse saw on-and-off success when fished in the middle of the water column.

When trolling spoons in 100 to 200 feet of water, lake trout were caught at Raynolds Reef, Spectacle Reef, and the northeast points of Bois Blanc Island. Chinook salmon were caught with spoons, meat rigs, and flasher-fly combinations in those same areas. Salmon were reported staging at the mouth of the Cheboygan River.
From the State Street drawbridge to the Cheboygan Dam spillway, smallmouth bass and rock bass were caught while drifting nightcrawlers. Other effective baits included spinnerbaits and swimbaits.

Anglers targeting lake trout reported decent fishing on the humps in 115 to 150 feet of water while trolling spoons and Spin-N-Glos in the bottom 30 feet of the water column. Walleye were scattered from 60 to 150 feet of water, with anglers targeting the top 30 to 40 feet of the water column. Anglers caught walleye on smaller spoons while trolling at slower speeds. A few steelhead were taken by anglers trolling spoons.
Anglers fishing off the pier and catwalk did well on channel catfish while using nightcrawlers and pyramid weights. A few nice smallmouth bass were caught by anglers casting tubes.

Lake trout fishing was good for anglers heading out to the reef. Spoons and Spin-N-Glos took fish. A few steelhead were taken on 3- to 7-color leadcore while trolling spoons, with orange working well. Good numbers of walleye were scattered from 60 to 150 feet of water. Anglers caught walleye 20 to 40 feet down while using smaller spoons and trolling at slower speeds. Northern pike were caught in the harbor by anglers casting spinners and spoons.

Salmon fishing improved, though water temperatures remained very warm. Adult Chinook salmon were caught, though the bite was not aggressive and was limited to short windows early in the morning and late in the evening. Meat rigs performed best in the warmer water, with productive depths ranging from 40 to 90 feet down throughout the water column. Anglers used an assortment of bait, including spoons, J-Plugs, meat rigs, and attractors paired with flies or squids. Effective colors included greens, blues, whites, UV, and glow patterns during low-light hours. Where cooler water or a thermocline was present, lake trout, steelhead, and juvenile salmon were also caught. Walleye were caught incidentally when trolling for salmon and trout; anglers targeting walleye found success in the top 30 feet of the water column using deep-diving crankbaits or nightcrawler harnesses.

Fishing for silver fish remained slow, but lake trout were caught out deep near the hump. The most productive depths were 120+ feet down and near the bottom using spoons or attractors paired with Spin-N-Glos or Spin-N-Glo flies. Walleye anglers did well in the evening and after dark while trolling body baits or nightcrawler harnesses, with the best action found in 30 to 65 feet of water when fishing the top 35 feet of the water column.

Anglers targeting Chinook salmon reported catching them in 100 to 140 feet of water straight out and south of the port while trolling plugs, spoons, and flasher-fly combinations 60 to 80 feet down. Chinook salmon were also caught in 200 to 300 feet of water while fishing 50 to 90 feet down. A few coho salmon and steelhead were caught in the mix. Anglers fishing the piers reported slow action as warm water returned around the harbor.

Warm water moved back in and pushed fish deeper. Chinook salmon and coho salmon were caught out from the pumped storage project in 95 to 120 feet of water while trolling 40 to 80 feet down, and at Big Sable Point in 90 to 160 feet of water while fishing 40 to 80 feet down. Straight out and to the north, a few were caught in 55 to 70 feet of water while fishing near the bottom. Plugs, spoons, flies, and meat rigs all worked. Warm water kept action slow on the pier and in Pere Marquette Lake, though smallmouth bass were reported from the pier.
Anglers targeting salmon reported low numbers. The temperature break was reported near 55 to 70 feet down. Trolling spoons and meat rigs produced results.

Anglers targeting salmon reported slow catch rates. The temperature break was between 55 and 75 feet of water. Spoons and meat rigs produced results. Fishing early in the morning before sunrise produced better results than in the evening.

Anglers fishing out of Elk Rapids caught lake trout while trolling roughly 80 to 90 feet down in 100 to 140 feet of water. Cowbells along with white and green flasher-fly combinations worked well. Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught lake trout when trolling in 80 to 140 feet of water. Water temperatures throughout the bay hovered between 70 and 73 degrees. Smallmouth bass were caught in the Elk River.

Lake trout along with a few Chinook salmon were caught by those trolling in 100 to 120 feet of water along the west bank just north of Elmwood Marina. A mix of spoons and flasher-fly combinations worked well. Anglers trolling near the Red #6 Buoy in 100 to 120 feet of water landed a few lake trout. Water temperatures hovered between 69 and 73 degrees.

Boat anglers trolling for salmon reported great numbers of fish at North Manitou Island. Anglers reported the best action in 130 to 300 feet of water, running baits 60 to 90 feet down. Boat anglers started a northbound troll on the southeast side of the island and followed the banks, marking heavy concentrations of bait fish. Steelhead were also caught 40 to 60 feet down. Anglers working both the first and second banks harvested a few Chinook salmon while trolling. Effective presentations included green and blue spoons, along with both natural and artificial meat rigs. Water temperatures were in the mid-60s down to 70 feet of water, dropping to 45 degrees below that depth. The best fishing occurred before sunrise and just before sunset.

Chinook salmon numbers were reported as very good straight out front and while trolling north. Anglers set lines 70 to 120 feet down during the early mornings and late evenings. Some anglers moved out to deeper water as water temperatures rose. Spoons remained the most popular lure choice, with the Bloody Nose pattern working best. Steelhead were also reported in the top 30 feet of the water column with orange spoons working best. Coho salmon numbers picked up for anglers who found bait pods.

Anglers running straight out to 240 to 300 feet of water and setting lines in the top 120 feet reported moderate numbers of Chinook salmon and a few coho salmon in the early morning before sunrise. Ten-color leadcore setups with flasher-fly combinations and magnum glow spoons worked best.
Fishing for panfish was great across the chain, with multiple anglers catching limits of very large bluegill from both shore and boats. Northern pike fishing also picked up.

Fishing for bass and panfish was good to great. Multiple anglers reported good bass fishing after sunrise in the morning. Some limits of quality bluegill were caught, along with a few decent northern pike.
Walleye fishing was good in the late evening. Bluegill and rock bass were caught in good numbers below Rogers Dam.
Fishing was very good from kayaks and from shore, with multiple panfish and bass caught. Most anglers targeted the channels.
Anglers reported success for anglers targeting smallmouth bass on the Muskegon River downstream from Croton Dam. Bluegill and bass fishing was phenomenal on inland waters.

Lake Michigan provided great fishing for Chinook salmon from Little Sable Point to the Silver Lake Sand Dunes. A drop in water temperature brought Chinook salmon into shallower water. Anglers began trolling in 60 feet of water before sunrise and pushed out to 180 feet of water as the day progressed. Spoons and J-Plugs were productive. Inland fishing remained slow.
Very few salmon entered the Pere Marquette River system. Anglers experienced good catches of salmon on Lake Michigan.

Anglers targeting walleye reported an uptick in action, catching decent numbers of fish near drop-offs and flats. Anglers reported good fishing during both the morning and evening. Some cast for them primarily near the bottom, while others trolled worm harnesses at slow speeds.
Yellow perch anglers reported good fishing, with the overall catch increasing dramatically. Most of the perch measured 8 to 11 inches, although some larger fish were reported.

Boat anglers did well on lake trout when trolling and jigging around Grand Island and Wood Island. Anglers trolling the bay reported a few Chinook salmon and coho salmon along with a few splake. Anglers fishing off the Anna River reported a slow bite on splake.

The river saw a fair amount of angling effort over the past week. Low catches of walleye were reported, with jigging serving as the preferred method for most anglers. Shore anglers reported catches of walleye, rock bass, and an occasional lake sturgeon in very low numbers. Early morning hours proved to be the most productive time of day for catching these fish.

Angling effort from Ontonagon increased slightly over the past week. Effort from the Silver City and Union Bay access sites also increased slightly but remained lower than in Ontonagon. Anglers reported catches consisting primarily of lake trout in fair-to-low numbers. Brown trout were also reported by anglers, but with much lower frequency. Anglers trolled depths ranging from 70 to 150 feet to find fish.

Angling effort was low from the harbor over the past week. Angler reports indicated catches of lake trout in low numbers, with boats trolling depths ranging from 60 to 160 feet to locate fish. Shore anglers fishing within harbor boundaries found little success.
Chinook salmon anglers trolling spoons off St. Martins Island and the Coast Guard pier reported low catches of salmon. Reports also indicated salmon were staging at the Carp River.
Boat anglers did well on lake trout when trolling and jigging at deeper depths.

Anglers targeting Chinook salmon out of Manistique reported good fishing south of the port and near the Garden Peninsula. Anglers reported good numbers of fish caught, including some individuals around 20 pounds. Spoons were the most common lure trolled.

Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks out toward north of Granite Rock and the Clay Banks in 120 to 160 feet of water for lake trout, catching fish throughout the water column. Good sized lake trout were also caught out near White Rocks.
A few anglers reported catching salmon and brown trout near Little Presque Isle and the Clay Banks in 60 to 100 feet of water, along with a few steelhead in slightly shallower depths. Few anglers headed out to Sand River and Shot Point, resulting in lower lake trout catches compared to previous early August reports. Prior to the weekend, some coho salmon were reported in 60 feet of water between the Lower Harbor Lighthouse and the Chocolay River, with lines set 25 to 30 feet down.

Fishing effort remained light in the Au Train area. Anglers fished depths consistent with previous weeks, working 120 to 160 feet of water. Lake trout were caught near the bottom northwest of Au Train Island and around Wood Island Reef.

Anglers reported poor-to-fair fishing over the past week, with a mixed bag consisting mostly of lake trout along with a few coho salmon, splake, and Chinook salmon. Trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations yielded the most success, while jigging for lake trout produced a slow bite. Anglers jigging reported better success using natural baits in water deeper than 150 feet.
Fishing activity slowed down with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers did best jigging in 15 to 20 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations near the bottom in 90 to 120 feet of water reported fair-to-good numbers of lake trout. Anglers also reported coho salmon, steelhead, and small Chinook salmon caught while trolling. Anglers targeting lake trout reported a fair bite when using natural and artificial baits, with most fish caught between 100 to 140 feet of water with some anglers finding success in water deeper than 200 feet.

Salmon fishing on the Great Lakes is really hitting its stride as many species are getting ready to begin their upstream migration. At the moment Lake Michigan is particularly popular for Chinook salmon with anglers trying various techniques to land this prized sportfish.
One tactic that can be particularly useful when targeting Chinook is fishing with glow lures. This species can often be caught near the surface in low-light conditions and glow lures make that opportunity even more appealing.
In particular, glow lures work well in the early morning hours before the sun comes up or at night. Many believe this type of lure attracts salmon because it can be seen in the dark from longer distances and encourages them to strike.
Are you interested in targeting Chinook salmon this late summer/early fall? Learn more at Michigan.gov/FishID .
This report is intended to give you an idea of what is going on around the state. Updates come from Fisheries staff and conservation officers. With nearly 11,000 inland lakes, the Great Lakes and thousands of miles of rivers and streams, not all locations can be listed. However, it is safe to say if a species is being caught in some waters in the area, they are likely being caught in all waters in that section of the state that have that species.

Yellow perch and walleye fishing remained very slow. Heavy rain and high winds restricted angler access and degraded water clarity across the lake, while a harmful algae bloom continued to spread. Yellow perch catch rates were reportedly very low. However, anglers targeting smallmouth and largemouth bass in local channels experienced strong results using soft plastics, particularly in areas north of Lake Erie Metropark.
Over the past week, fishing was very slow, with only a few yellow perch caught on the east side of Spoils Island in 15 feet of water.

Fishing was generally slow due to high winds across all areas. A few yellow perch were caught near the Spark Plug mark in the shipping channel midweek. Boat anglers also caught a few largemouth bass over the weekend in Sunset Marina while casting various artificial baits.

Boat anglers caught a few mature Chinook salmon while trolling in the basin and off the breakwalls. Glow and chrome/red-head plugs were most effective. Pier anglers also landed a few Chinook salmon while casting glow spoons.

Chinook salmon and coho salmon were caught 35 to 90 feet down in 100 to 170 feet of water. Orange and green spoons as well as green flies were effective. A few Chinook salmon were caught off the pierheads on glow plugs, while pier anglers landed a few salmon casting spoons.
Pier fishing remained decent. Most Chinook and coho salmon were caught by anglers casting spoons and spinners. Boat anglers experienced slower fishing, with most boats staying near the piers.

Pier fishing was fair, with anglers catching a decent number of Chinook salmon on crankbaits. Fishing pressure remained high. Boat anglers caught a few salmon while trolling the pierheads, and the anglers fishing in approximately 100 feet of water had good mixed-bag catches.

Boat anglers fishing the lower river caught a few salmon, though fishing was generally slow. Fishing conditions near the Berrien Springs Dam were similar, with anglers catching a few salmon amidst overall slow activity.
Shore anglers caught Chinook salmon and coho salmon while casting spoons. A few fish were also taken by anglers trolling.

Fishing remained slow overall, and windy weather kept boat anglers off the water. Anglers fishing from the pier in Tawas caught rock bass, largemouth bass, and an occasional walleye. A few salmon were caught out of the Tawas River, while channel catfish and an occasional walleye were landed in the Au Gres River.

High winds hampered angler effort over the past week. When anglers were able to get out, a mixed bag of Chinook salmon, Atlantic salmon, walleye, and occasional steelhead was caught. The best results were in 30 to 50 feet of water throughout Thunder Bay. Spoons in a variety of colors were productive throughout the water column.

Anglers had success targeting Chinook salmon while drifting spawn and beads near the 9th Street Dam throughout the day. Casting stickbaits and spoons was also productive in the evening and after dark. Boat anglers had some success trolling deep-diving crankbaits and spoons. A few Atlantic salmon and coho salmon were taken as well.

Anglers at the Cheboygan Dam spillway primarily caught Chinook salmon, along with an occasional coho salmon, pink salmon, or steelhead. Catch rates varied daily. Rain early in the week brought a fair push of salmon to the dam, where anglers caught up to three salmon per day. The bite slowed significantly as the week progressed, with weekend anglers averaging fewer than one fish per trip.
Salmon and trout were taken on cast small spoons and minnow-style crankbaits, as well as drifted or bottom-bounced beads and spawn. Small walleye, smallmouth bass, and rock bass were also caught between the Cheboygan Dam and the State Street drawbridge while floating nightcrawlers.

Adult chinook salmon were present in good numbers in 20 to 30 feet of water off Swan Bay, though the bite was late. Anglers trolled plugs and body baits off planer boards.
Outside the bay, up the lake, and straight out from the harbor, anglers caught lake trout, immature Chinook salmon, and an occasional steelhead, coho salmon, or walleye. Successful anglers ran lines throughout the water column near baitfish. Spoons in standard and slim sizes were the most effective lures. Productive colors included white, green, blue, orange, yellow, and glow patterns during early morning and late evening hours.

Angling effort was light due to rough, windy weather. When anglers were able to get out, lake trout were caught off Stoneport and between the lighthouses. An occasional Chinook salmon was also caught off Stoneport, False Presque Isle, and off the Grand River outlet north of the marina. Steelhead, coho salmon, and walleye were caught on occasion. The most productive depths were 45 to 80 feet of water, with lines run throughout the water column. Anglers fished a mix of J-plugs and spoons in white, green, blue, orange, and glow patterns early in the morning and late in the day.

Pier fishing remained slow, with very few Chinook salmon reported over the weekend. Anglers caught a small number of Chinook salmon from the pier using spoons and jigging spoons. On Lake Michigan, anglers targeting Chinook salmon found fish in 90 to 250 feet of water while trolling 40 to 80 feet down with plugs and spoons, along with a few coho salmon and steelhead in the mix. Anglers also reported a few salmon from the channel and Manistee Lake, as well as northern pike and smallmouth bass.

Pier fishing remained very slow. Anglers trolling for Chinook salmon off Big Sable Point caught fish in 140 to 170 feet of water while running plugs 45 to 80 feet down. Most salmon were scattered throughout the water column.

Boat anglers targeting salmon reported low catch numbers despite marking a decent number of fish. Water temperature rose, holding around 80 feet down. Anglers targeting salmon near Medusa Creek reported slow action while trolling and drifting skein.

Anglers targeting salmon in the Bear River reported salmon and an occasional steelhead while fishing beads, flies, and skein. Anglers fishing off the piers and breakwall in Petoskey reported slow but steady action casting spoons in the early morning. Boat anglers trolled primarily in 30 feet of water or less using plugs and body baits. The thermocline was reported around 80 feet down.

Anglers fishing out of Elk Rapids caught lake trout while trolling 80 feet down in 110 to 140 feet of water. A few ciscoes were also caught, with most caught higher in the water column around 45 feet down. Anglers heading south of the Center Road launch caught mixed bags of lake trout, cisco, and salmon while trolling in 80 to 140 feet of water.

Boat activity was minimal. Anglers targeted Chinook salmon on the first bank with little success. Water temperatures near the harbor pierhead were in the low 60s, with a few salmon entering the harbor. Pier anglers had the best success catching Chinook salmon before sunrise while floating skein.

Mature Chinook salmon were still landed out front and off the shelf in 120 to 160 feet of water, but overall numbers remained low due to warm water temperatures. Anglers jigging as well as pier anglers reported low catch numbers, as most Chinook salmon moved into the Betsie River. In Platte Bay, coho salmon fishing was moderate for anglers jigging skein near the bottom.

Boat anglers began targeting yellow perch in Suttons Bay, Omena Bay, and Northport. A few anglers had successful trips when using natural bait. Lake trout anglers were trolling near Ballenger Creek in depths ranging from 80 to 120 feet of water.

Walleye fishing was fair to good. Anglers caught fish casting jigs tipped with live bait or artificial bait featuring glow paint, using erratic, darting presentations to trigger strikes. Anglers trolling reported success using crawler harnesses or slender diving baits. Yellow perch fishing yielded mixed results with some anglers near the Escanaba River and harbor having successful outings, locating schools remained difficult. Minnows fished along deep-water structures and flats produced the best results. Coho salmon were frequently observed, but action was generally slow. Trolling artificial lures such as spoons and crankbaits yielded little success, and anglers using forward-facing sonar while jigging also encountered a tough bite. Early morning and low-light periods near or after dark offered the best opportunity for coho salmon.

Boat anglers reported catching a few coho salmon and splake while trolling the bay. Anglers fishing off the mouth of the Anna River also caught splake and a few coho salmon. Spawn and spinners were the most effective baits.

Over the past week, the river saw minimal angling effort. Anglers reported low catches of walleye, primarily caught by jigging. Trolling proved largely ineffective. Inclement weather throughout the week hindered overall fishing conditions.

The access sites at Ontonagon, Silver City, and Union Bay each saw low angling effort over the past week. High winds and frequent rain showers continued to limit lake access on multiple days. However, fair-weather days produced good fishing, with anglers reporting solid catches of lake trout along with lesser numbers of coho salmon. Fish were taken by trolling across depths ranging from 40 to 150 feet.

The harbor saw low angling effort over the past week due to inclement weather limiting lake access. When conditions allowed, anglers reported mixed catches of brown trout, steelhead, coho salmon, and lake trout in low to fair numbers. Lake trout comprised most of these catches. Fish were taken by trolling in depths ranging from 30 to 150 feet.

Following early-week rain, some additional Chinook salmon moved into the Carp River and the mouth of Nunns Creek. Anglers caught up to two fish per trip when casting small spoons and minnow-style crankbaits, or drifting spawn. The bite slowed heading into the weekend, with anglers experiencing low success rates despite significant effort. Pink salmon were reported in the rapids upstream of the Carp River fishing pier near the river mouth.
Fishing activity was slow, though boat anglers reported success targeting lake trout when jigging and trolling. Anglers fishing off the breakwall reported a slow salmon bite.

River anglers reported catching pink salmon and Chinook salmon. A small run of Chinook salmon entered the river, with fish observed near the mouth and up near the dam. Anglers trolling and casting crankbaits downstream of the paper mill and rapids reported occasional catches, though Chinook salmon fishing was slower overall. Shore anglers landed a few fish drifting skein, egg sacs, and beads, while other anglers caught fish casting shallow-running crankbaits during low-light periods at dusk and into the night.

Most anglers continued to troll north of White Rocks toward Granite Rock and the Clay Banks in 80 to 160 feet of water for lake trout. Anglers reported catching lake trout throughout the water column, primarily near the bottom using downriggers. A few anglers trolling near the mouth of the Chocolay and Carp rivers from Lower Harbor caught coho salmon, Chinook salmon, and brown trout at depths around 30 feet in 60 feet of water. Catch rates appeared to increase as water temperatures cooled.

Angler participation increased out of Au Train on calm weather days. Lake trout fishing was productive, with several angler limits. Trolling near the bottom in 140 to 180 feet of water out toward the Flats northeast of Au Train Island yielded steady success. Anglers jigging near the bottom off Au Train Island in 40 to 80 feet of water landed lean lake trout weighing 7 to 10 pounds. Anglers targeting brown trout and salmon in 40 to 60 feet of water marked numerous fish on electronics, though no catches were reported. Activity near river mouths and Scott Falls is expected to increase over the coming weeks as water temperatures cool.

Anglers reported fair fishing, with catches consisting of coho salmon, lake trout, and splake, along with a few larger Chinook salmon taken by trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations. Anglers jigging for lake trout experienced fair action using both natural and artificial presentations in 100 to 140 feet of water. Shore fishing remained slow, though anglers casting from shore managed to catch a few coho salmon.
Fishing activity slowed, with most anglers targeting walleye and yellow perch. Anglers had the best success jigging in 15 to 20 feet of water using natural bait.

Anglers reported fair to good lake trout fishing while trolling spoons and flasher-fly combinations around structure in 50 to 100 feet of water. A few coho salmon and steelhead were also caught while trolling, though overall numbers remained low. Anglers jigging for lake trout reported good action when using natural presentations, with most fish caught in 80 to 120 feet of water.

Anglers in the Les Cheneaux area caught yellow perch in the Cedarville and Government Bay areas, sorting through smaller fish to keep a full limit. Very few splake were present in the Hessel area. Smallmouth bass fishing was good around the islands near Hessel. In DeTour, when weather permitted, anglers had good success trolling for lake trout on the flats while also taking a few pink salmon.

Autumn can be one of the best times of year to seek out your favorite fish species for a day of fun angling. Several species to target this October and November include walleye, perch and trout.
Walleye are thought to be in their best condition in the fall and can often be found in the river mouth areas of larger, inland lakes. They’re gathering there to take advantage of baitfish that like to hang out as the weather cools off. Set your sights on 10 to 12 feet deep to find these guys.
Perch will also populate around these same river-mouths, but these fish will likely be much closer to the river than walleye. Check out depths as shallow as 4 feet to find them.
Trout will be available in some of these larger lakes as well during this time period and can be found in the same areas as the walleye and perch.
Try your luck at some great angling this fall. For more information on the numerous opportunities to fish this autumn, visit Michigan.gov/Fishing .
